source_title: Docker Hodgepodge Images
claim_summary: Chainguard staff post rebuts a Docker blog that criticised vendors shipping their own Linux distributions, arguing Docker also ships its own distro
limitation: Vendor-vs-vendor argument; not a product change. A Hacker News commenter (E0, user opinion) argued the post misunderstands how image scanners work; neither side was independently tested here

source_title: Chainguard and Cursor partner to bring secure open source artifacts to agentic coding
claim_summary: Announces partnership positioning Chainguard Containers and Libraries (Python, JavaScript, Java) as the open source source-of-trust for Cursor users pulling from the Chainguard Repository
feature: AI coding agent to hardened artifact registry integration
availability: partnership announced; marketplace plugin shipped later (2026-06-24)
limitation: Requires both Chainguard and Cursor subscriptions; Axios coverage not fetched (robots.txt unreadable, HTTP 403) and The New Stack coverage not fetched (robots.txt disallows Claude agents); no independent confirmation read

source_title: Chainguard customers safe from new npm worm and xinference supply chain attack
claim_summary: Vendor states customers were not affected by an npm worm (22 libraries) and three malicious xinference PyPI versions (2.6.0-2.6.2), because Chainguard builds from public source and refuses packages that depend on install-time scripts
limitation: Customer-safety claim is the vendor's own; no independent audit of the build refusal or of customer exposure; attribution to a threat group stated as pending in the post

source_title: Going beyond CVEs: Chainguard's one day KEV SLA
claim_summary: Any CVE added to the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog that affects a Chainguard container image is to be remediated within one calendar day, for Containers customers with a CVE SLA
availability: contractual SLA for existing CVE-SLA customers
limitation: Vendor also claims <20-hour average for Critical CVEs and 2-day median across severities; no independent measurement; SLA terms (exclusions, remedies) not read

source_title: Chainguard EKS add-ons are now available in the AWS Marketplace
claim_summary: FIPS 140-3 validated, zero-known-CVE images for EKS add-ons (kube-proxy, CoreDNS, VPC CNI, EBS CSI, EFS CSI) listed in AWS Marketplace as drop-in replacements
limitation: 'Only third-party provider' is a vendor claim; AWS Marketplace listing not fetched; 'zero-known-CVE' depends on scanner and date

source_title: malcontent v1.23.0
claim_summary: Adds rule category filtering and a dated false-positive-reduction rules pass; one of 26 in-window releases (v1.22.0 2026-04-15 to v1.27.1 2026-10-07)
limitation: Recurring 'FPR' rule updates show false positives are an ongoing maintenance cost; no published precision/recall

product: Chainguard OS / Containers RPM compatibility; FINOS membership
source_title: Chainguard brings first-party RHEL 9 and RHEL 10 RPM support to Chainguard OS, joins FINOS
claim_summary: Announces RPM compatibility for first-party packages built for RHEL 9 and RHEL 10 inside Chainguard Containers on Chainguard OS, and membership of the Fintech Open Source Foundation
feature: RHEL RPM compatibility in hardened images
availability: preview (the 2026-06-24 containers update describes RHEL 9/10 RPM support as 'in preview')
limitation: Compatibility scope and licensing of RHEL-built packages not examined; FINOS membership not confirmed on a FINOS page

source_title: Luck isn't a security control: What happened with mini Shai-Hulud and what you need to do
claim_summary: Vendor states a new npm supply chain worm hit 400+ packages in 24 hours and that Chainguard customers were not affected
limitation: Package count and customer-safety claim are vendor statements; npm/GitHub advisories for the campaign were not cross-checked; one of several 2026 incident posts (others listed in search log)

product: Company direction (forking open source at scale)
source_title: The hardest fork
claim_summary: CEO argues frontier-model vulnerability discovery (Mythos) is real and that Chainguard is building infrastructure to fork, maintain and distribute thousands of open source projects under time pressure
limitation: Opinion and intention; no committed scope, timeline or licence model; devops.com critical piece ('Can Chainguard Save Open-Source Software from Mythos? Can Anyone?') returned a 403 challenge and was not read

product: Chainguard Libraries for JavaScript malware/greyware scanner
source_title: The expanding threat landscape: Chainguard now scans source code for traditional malware and greyware
claim_summary: New source-code scanner for npm packages requested through the Libraries upstream fallback; vendor says it scans 100,000+ packages a day and has blocked 52,000+ packages as malware or 'greyware'
feature: malware and greyware scanning at the registry
availability: shipped for npm upstream fallback; other ecosystems 'soon'
limitation: Proprietary scanner; no published false-positive rate, test set or definition audit of 'greyware'; The New Stack coverage not fetched (robots.txt disallows Claude agents)

source_title: Faster than the advisory
claim_summary: Vendor case study: an Argo CD security fix was picked up by Factory automation 77 minutes after the upstream release and was in Wolfi six days before GitHub's global advisory database caught up (May 7)
limitation: Single vendor-selected example; the GitHub advisory publication date and Wolfi package timestamps were not independently re-checked

source_title: /C O R R E C T I O N -- Chainguard/ Chainguard Launches Athena, the Industry Coalition to Fix Open Source Vulnerabilities Before Attackers Can Find Them
claim_summary: Launches Athena, a coalition with founding members including BNY, Cisco, Cloudflare, Docker, JPMorganChase and PwC, to pool AI-discovered open source vulnerabilities, remediate under embargo and push fixes upstream; claims 20,000+ findings processed and 2,000+ patches across 500 projects
feature: vulnerability clearinghouse; pre-disclosure patched forks via Chainguard Libraries
availability: operational per vendor; membership by application
limitation: Release was re-issued as a correction (what changed is not stated); Infosecurity Magazine dates the announcement 2026-06-16; pre-embargo fixes go to members first, which is an access asymmetry; first disclosure wave promised for 'next month' actually began 2026-09-28; Bloomberg and ZDNet coverage not fetched (robots.txt disallows Claude agents)

source_title: Chainguard Agent Skills is now open to everyone, with a private registry to manage your internal skills
claim_summary: Agent Skills beta opened to all users with 1,000+ hardened community skills, a private registry for internal skills, and a closed beta for hardening first-party skills
feature: hardened agent-skill catalog and private skill registry
limitation: Hardening criteria are vendor-defined; public chainguard-dev/cg-skills repo (Apache-2.0, created 2026-06-22) exists but catalog contents and review quality were not audited; The New Stack coverage not fetched (robots.txt)

source_title: Introducing the Chainguard cinc-auditor image: STIG scanning for Chainguard Containers, ready to run
claim_summary: Releases a container image of the open source InSpec-compatible cinc-auditor scanner bundling Chainguard's GPOS SRG InSpec profile, tested end-to-end with Anchore Enterprise
limitation: Anchore testing claim not checked on an Anchore source; profile licence not examined

source_title: Request for clarification of the future of Wolfi
claim_summary: Community users report many package definitions (e.g. spark, keycloak, karpenter, kyverno and a long list of cloud-native packages) moved from public Wolfi to a private enterprise repository via merges on 2026-06-09 and 2026-06-11; a Chainguard member replied 2026-07-10 that Wolfi aims only to cover packages needed for the free Chainguard Containers and pointed users to the free Catalog Starter
feature: reduction of package set in the public Wolfi repository
limitation: Removal list compiled by issue participants, not re-derived here; commits checked via GitHub API (2026-06-09 merge: 29 files, 4,128 deletions; 2026-06-11 merge: 139 files); a user-claimed link to a competitor's free tier is speculation (E0); wolfi-dev/.github FAQ updated 2026-07-10

source_title: Chainguard Libraries for Java is now GA; CVE remediation beta available for sign up
claim_summary: Libraries for Java declared GA; CVE remediation (backported fixes, starting with Spring Boot ecosystem: spring-boot, spring-framework, spring-security, h2database) in beta
feature: Java dependencies built from source; backported CVE fixes
limitation: Backported forks diverge from upstream release lines (reuse/maintenance trade-off); no independent test of patch correctness; The New Stack coverage not fetched (robots.txt)

source_title: Secure your pipelines with Chainguard Actions, now available in Open Beta
claim_summary: Chainguard Actions (hardened replacements for popular GitHub Actions) opens to self-serve open beta, with one-day SLA for requested Actions and a migration skill that inventories and migrates workflow usage
feature: hardened GitHub Actions catalog; agent migration skill
limitation: Replacing upstream Actions with vendor copies moves trust rather than removing it; no independent review of the hardened Actions

product: Chainguard plugin for Cursor; Chainguard power for Kiro
source_title: Chainguard plug-in now available on Cursor Marketplace
claim_summary: Cursor Marketplace plugin gives Cursor agents access to the Chainguard Repository (images; Python, Java, JavaScript dependencies); a companion post the same day describes a Kiro 'power' that swaps public base images and packages for Chainguard ones
feature: agent IDE plugins for hardened artifacts
limitation: GitHub API: chainguard-dev/chainguard-cursor-plugin licence NOASSERTION and chainguard-dev/chainguard-kiro-power no detected licence (2026-10-16), so reuse rights are unclear; plugin behaviour not executed

source_title: This Shit is Hard: How AI keeps our code on standard
claim_summary: Vendor reports a fleet of single-purpose AI agents opened more than 4,700 standards-fix pull requests over 8 weeks and auto-merged 75% of those judged low-risk, with deterministic CI gates deciding auto-merge
limitation: Self-reported internal metrics; denominator of rejected/reverted PRs and defect escape rate not given; follow-up post 2026-07-02 describes monitoring dashboards

product: Chainguard Repository policies; Chainguard Libraries for JavaScript
source_title: Chainguard Repository adds new policies, Chainguard Libraries for JavaScript is GA
claim_summary: Malware/greyware scanning extended from npm to upstream Python, Java packages and container images; policy engine extended to those artifacts (new policy types in open beta); upstream fallback with cooldown for Java and Python; Libraries for JavaScript GA
availability: JavaScript Libraries GA; policy types open beta
limitation: '70+ greyware projects' blocked per week is vendor-reported; SiliconANGLE 'exclusive' restates vendor claims rather than testing them

source_title: Fewer CVEs, more accurate findings: Wiz now scans Chainguard Libraries for Python and Java
claim_summary: Wiz can now scan Chainguard Libraries for Python and Java, recognising Chainguard-built packages to reduce vulnerability noise (Upwind announced Python Libraries scanning on 2026-05-26)
limitation: Scanner false-positive reduction is claimed, not measured here; no Wiz-side source read

source_title: The State of Trusted Open Source: June 2026
claim_summary: Vendor reports 886 distinct CVEs remediated across its image projects in March-May 2026 (vs 377 the prior quarter and 154 in its December 2025 report), with over 63% high-severity
limitation: Vendor-defined counting; catalog grew over the same period so counts are not normalised; no independent dataset

source_title: We're putting our security to the test, and we want your help

limitation: Outcome (findings, payouts) not found in window; Bugcrowd page not read

source_title: Expanding Athena
claim_summary: Three weeks after launch, vendor says Athena has processed 40,000+ vulnerabilities (42% critical/high), adds members (Akamai, Black Duck, Cycode, JFrog, Morgan Stanley, Qualys, Upwind, Zafran) and hands fixes to the Linux Foundation's Akrites for upstream disclosure
limitation: Intake counts are not verified; same-day PR Newswire release is a duplicate; Akrites not checked on a Linux Foundation page

claim_summary: Vendor analysis: a privileged token stolen via a misconfigured pull_request_target workflow was used to publish five trojanized versions across four @asyncapi npm packages
limitation: Third-party incident; download estimates vary by source per the post; AsyncAPI's own postmortem not read

source_title: Booz Allen Hamilton signs enterprise license agreement with Chainguard
claim_summary: Enterprise license agreement gives more than 6,000 Booz Allen engineers access to Chainguard Containers and Libraries for government programs
limitation: Access is not usage; no Booz Allen-side source read; licence counts are not adoption evidence

limitation: False-positive suppression relies on vendor-authored advisories (a shift of trust to the vendor's data); NeuVector-side source not read

feature: planned external availability of internal sandbox, harness and CI

feature: FIPS 140-3 validated crypto module with hybrid PQ key exchange

source_title: Athena's disclosures begin
